question: What is the purpose of Alabama's Real Estate Recovery Fund under Ala. Code § 34-27-31?
choice_a: To pay licensees' annual errors-and-omissions insurance premiums
choice_b: To allow an aggrieved party to recover actual or compensatory damages sustained in Alabama as a result of a broker's or salesperson's violation of the license law or commission rules
choice_c: To reimburse brokerages for unpaid commissions owed by defaulting clients
choice_d: To fund the Alabama Real Estate Commission's general operating budget
explanation: Ala. Code § 34-27-31(a) establishes the Recovery Fund so an aggrieved party may recover actual or compensatory damages -- not interest or court costs -- sustained within Alabama as a result of a broker's or salesperson's violation of Article 1 or 2 of the license law, or of commission rules.

question: Under Ala. Code § 34-27-31, what may an aggrieved party NOT collect from the Recovery Fund even after winning a valid judgment?
choice_d: The unpaid principal amount of the judgment
explanation: Section 34-27-31(a) limits recovery from the fund to actual or compensatory damages, expressly excluding interest and court costs.

question: When a person applies for an original Alabama real estate broker or salesperson license, what fee must be paid into the Recovery Fund in addition to all other license fees?
explanation: Ala. Code § 34-27-31(c)(1) requires an applicant for an original broker or salesperson license to pay a $30 fee for deposit into the Recovery Fund, in addition to all other required fees.

question: If the Alabama Real Estate Commission does not issue a license after an applicant has paid the Recovery Fund fee with the original application, what happens to that fee?
choice_a: It is returned to the applicant
choice_b: It is forfeited and kept in the Recovery Fund
choice_c: It is transferred to the general license examination fee
choice_d: It is held for two years and then forfeited
explanation: Section 34-27-31(c)(1) specifically provides that if the commission does not issue the license, the Recovery Fund fee paid with the application is returned to the applicant.

question: A salesperson who already paid the Recovery Fund fee later becomes licensed as a broker and pays the broker's additional Recovery Fund fee. What happens under § 34-27-31(c)(2)?
choice_a: Both fees are permanently retained by the fund with no refund available
choice_b: Upon request, one of the two fees is refunded, and no additional fee is ever required again upon attaining broker status
choice_c: The licensee must pay a third, higher fee to reconcile the two payments
choice_d: The salesperson-level fee is automatically forfeited and non-refundable
explanation: Section 34-27-31(c)(2) provides that a salesperson who paid the fee and later becomes a broker (paying the broker's additional fee) is refunded one of the fees upon request, and no salesperson licensee is required to pay an additional fee upon attaining broker status.

question: How often must a licensee make the Recovery Fund payment described as being made "in lieu of bond" under § 34-27-31(c)(3)?
choice_b: Every time the licensee changes qualifying brokers
choice_c: Only one time, when originally licensed by the commission
explanation: Section 34-27-31(c)(3) states that payments made to the Recovery Fund in lieu of bond by a licensee are paid only one time, when the person is originally licensed by the commission.

question: Under Ala. Code § 34-27-31(d), what triggers a commission order requiring every active broker and salesperson to pay an additional $30 per license into the Recovery Fund?
choice_b: The fund receiving three or more claims in one year
choice_c: The state legislature's biennial budget review
explanation: Section 34-27-31(d) provides that when the Recovery Fund balance falls below $500,000, the commission may order each broker and salesperson to pay an additional $30 per license into the fund to replenish it.

question: Under § 34-27-31(d), is a licensee on inactive status required to contribute to a Recovery Fund replenishment assessment?
choice_a: No, but a $30 fee is due at the time the license is later activated
choice_b: Yes, inactive licensees must pay the same $30 assessment as active licensees
choice_c: No, and no fee will ever be required from that licensee again
choice_d: Yes, but only if the licensee has an unresolved consumer complaint on file
explanation: Section 34-27-31(d) exempts a licensee on inactive status from contributing to a replenishment assessment at that time, but requires payment of the $30 fee when the license is later activated.

question: Under Ala. Code § 34-27-31(b)(2), what is the maximum aggregate amount the Recovery Fund will pay out for claims based on judgments or settlements against any one licensee?
explanation: Section 34-27-31(b)(2) caps payments for claims based on judgments or settlements against any one person at $50,000 in the aggregate.

question: Under Ala. Code § 34-27-31(b)(3), what is the maximum aggregate amount the Recovery Fund will pay for claims arising out of the same real estate transaction, regardless of the number of claimants?
choice_d: An amount divided equally with no cap per transaction
explanation: Section 34-27-31(b)(3) caps payments for claims arising out of the same transaction at $25,000 in the aggregate, no matter how many claimants there are.

question: Under § 34-27-31(b)(1), the Recovery Fund is NOT obligated for a broker's acts or omissions in which of these situations?
choice_a: The broker represented a first-time homebuyer who is unrelated to the broker
choice_b: The broker represented the seller in a standard arm's-length residential sale
choice_c: The broker was a newly licensed salesperson at the time of the violation
choice_d: The broker was acting on his or her own behalf, or on behalf of a spouse, child, or parent, regarding property in which that broker or family member has or is attempting to acquire an interest
explanation: Section 34-27-31(b)(1) excludes fund liability for a broker's or salesperson's own transactions or those involving a spouse, child, or parent's property interest, along with claims from inactive licensees and time-share marketing/development acts.

question: Per Ala. Code § 34-27-31(b)(1), claims arising from a broker's or salesperson's acts or omissions connected with which activity are categorically excluded from Recovery Fund payment?
choice_a: Marketing or development of a time-sharing project
choice_b: Listing a single-family residence for sale
choice_d: Representing a buyer in a commercial lease
explanation: Section 34-27-31(b)(1) states the fund is not obligated for any judgment or settlement resulting from a broker's or salesperson's act or omission committed in conjunction with the marketing or development of a time-sharing project.

question: What must happen to a licensee whose conduct caused the commission to pay a claim or judgment from the Recovery Fund, under Ala. Code § 34-27-31(e)(6)?
choice_a: The licensee simply receives a formal reprimand with no financial or licensing consequence
choice_b: The commission may terminate all of the licensee's licenses and withhold a new license until the amount paid is repaid in full plus 12 percent annual interest
choice_c: The licensee's license is automatically renewed once the calendar year ends
choice_d: The licensee is permanently barred from ever holding any professional license in Alabama
explanation: Section 34-27-31(e)(6) allows the commission to terminate the licensee's licenses after a Recovery Fund payment and to refuse a new license until the licensee repays the fund in full plus 12 percent annual interest; a bankruptcy discharge does not relieve this obligation.

question: Does a discharge in bankruptcy relieve a licensee of the obligation to repay the Recovery Fund after the commission has paid a claim on the licensee's behalf?
choice_a: Yes, bankruptcy discharge automatically erases the repayment obligation
choice_b: Yes, but only if the licensee has already surrendered the license voluntarily
choice_c: No, § 34-27-31(e)(6) states a discharge in bankruptcy does not relieve the person from the penalties and disabilities imposed by the section
choice_d: No repayment is ever required regardless of bankruptcy status
explanation: Section 34-27-31(e)(6) explicitly provides that a discharge in bankruptcy does not relieve the licensee from the repayment penalties and disabilities described in the section.

question: If the Recovery Fund's balance is insufficient to satisfy a duly authorized claim, how does § 34-27-31(e)(7) direct the commission to handle payment once money becomes available?
choice_a: Pay only the largest claim first regardless of filing order
choice_b: Split all pending claims evenly regardless of amount owed or filing order
choice_c: Deny all claims filed while the fund balance was insufficient
choice_d: Pay the unpaid claims or portions, plus 12 percent annual interest, in the order the claims were originally filed
explanation: Section 34-27-31(e)(7) requires the commission, once sufficient money is deposited, to satisfy unpaid claims or portions plus 12 percent annual interest in the order the claims were originally filed.

question: Under Ala. Code § 34-27-31(e)(1), what must an aggrieved person do when commencing a lawsuit that may result in a claim against the Recovery Fund?
choice_a: Notify the commission in writing, by certified mail with return receipt requested, at the time the action is commenced
choice_b: Wait until final judgment before informing the commission of the lawsuit
choice_c: File the claim directly with the State Treasurer instead of the commission
choice_d: Publish notice of the lawsuit in a local newspaper
explanation: Section 34-27-31(e)(1) requires the aggrieved person to notify the commission in writing, by certified mail, return receipt requested, at the time the action seeking a judgment that may result in collection from the fund is commenced.

question: After a valid judgment is obtained and all appeals are concluded, what must the aggrieved person do to apply for payment out of the Recovery Fund under § 34-27-31(e)(3)?
choice_a: Simply request a check directly from the commission by phone
choice_b: File a verified claim in the court that entered the judgment and, after 10 days' written notice to the commission, apply to the court for an order directing payment from the fund
choice_c: Re-file the entire lawsuit against the Recovery Fund itself as a new defendant
choice_d: Submit the claim to the licensee's errors-and-omissions insurer instead of the court
explanation: Section 34-27-31(e)(3) requires the aggrieved person, after termination of all proceedings including appeals, to file a verified claim in the judgment court and, on 10 days' written notice to the commission, apply for a court order directing payment from the Recovery Fund.

question: Once the commission pays a sum from the Recovery Fund under a court order, what right does § 34-27-31(h) give the commission with respect to the underlying judgment?
choice_a: The commission gains no further rights and simply absorbs the loss
choice_b: The commission may only recover the funds through a new lawsuit against the aggrieved party
choice_c: The commission is subrogated to the rights of the judgment creditor, to the extent of the amount paid, and that interest in the judgment is assigned to the commission
choice_d: The judgment is automatically vacated once the fund pays the claim
explanation: Section 34-27-31(h) provides that when the commission pays a sum from the Recovery Fund on court order, it is subrogated to the judgment creditor's rights, title, and interest in the judgment to the extent of the amount paid, and that interest is assigned to the commission.

question: Where are funds collected under § 34-27-31 held, and by what name is the special fund known?
choice_a: Held in a private escrow account managed by the licensee's brokerage
choice_b: Deposited directly into the University of Alabama's general endowment
choice_c: Held by the National Association of Realtors on Alabama's behalf
choice_d: Deposited into the State Treasury and held in trust by the commission as the "Real Estate Recovery Fund"
explanation: Section 34-27-31(f) states that sums received under the section are deposited into the State Treasury and held by the commission in trust in a special fund known as the Real Estate Recovery Fund.
